claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few questions to help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

First, **is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?** For example, is he attending school, college doing A-levels or similar qualifications, or enrolled in an approved training program?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's in sixth form doing his A-levels at the local college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. 

**Can you confirm Alex's exact date of birth, or at least confirm whether he is still under 20 years old?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex and your living situation.

**Are you Alex's parent or the person responsible for him, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm his parent and he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. A few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - in Manchester actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** For example, Alex's other parent or another family member?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming it for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. One final question:

**Are you or your partner (if you have one) subject to immigration control, or are there any restrictions on your right to reside in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there are no immigration restrictions - I have the full right to live here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the eligibility criteria:

✓ Alex is 17 years old (under 20)
✓ He's in full-time non-advanced education (A-levels at sixth form)
✓ You're his parent and he lives with you
✓ You live in the UK
✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
✓ You have the right to reside in the UK without immigration restrictions

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. Please note that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may be subject to the High Income Child Benefit Charge, which means you might have to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through your tax return. However, this doesn't affect your eligibility to claim it.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
